title: Exactness of homogeneous localization and degree-zero parts
statement: Let A be a commutative ring with a decomposition A=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}A_n into additive subgroups such that A_aA_b\subseteq A_{a+b}. A graded A-module is an A-module M with a decomposition M=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M_n into additive subgroups such that A_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}; an A-linear map u:M\to N of graded A-modules is degree-preserving if u(M_n)\subseteq N_n for every n. Let s\in A_d be homogeneous of degree d\ge0. For a graded A-module M let M_s=M[1/s] be its localization at the powers of s [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], graded by declaring m/s^k homogeneous of degree e-kd for m\in M_e, and let M_{(s)}\subseteq M_s be its degree-zero part, the elements m/s^k with m\in M_{kd}; a degree-preserving map u induces degree-preserving maps u_s:M_s\to N_s, m/s^k\mapsto u(m)/s^k, and their restrictions u_{(s)}:M_{(s)}\to N_{(s)}. If M'\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}M'' is an exact sequence of graded A-modules with degree-preserving maps (\operatorname{im}f=\ker g), then M'_s\to M_s\to M''_s and M'_{(s)}\to M_{(s)}\to M''_{(s)} are exact. Consequently any exact sequence (finite or infinite) of graded A-modules with degree-preserving maps stays exact after applying (-)_s and after applying (-)_{(s)}.

proof.text: Forget the gradings and apply exactness of localization at the multiplicative subset of powers of s, as stated by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. The induced sequence M'_s \to M_s \to M''_s is therefore exact.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MR proof, Mayer–Vietoris paragraph (localization exactness)

proof.text: The localization grading is preserved by f_s and g_s because f and g preserve degrees and s is homogeneous. Write an element of a localized module as a finite sum of homogeneous fractions. If a homogeneous degree-zero element y of M_s maps to zero in M''_s, exactness from Step 1 gives x in M'_s with f_s(x)=y; taking the degree-zero homogeneous component x_0 gives f_s(x_0)=y. Conversely, g_s(f_s(x))=0 holds for every x by exactness before taking components. Thus M'_{(s)} \to M_{(s)} \to M''_{(s)} is exact. The same argument applies in every degree, so it applies termwise to finite or infinite exact sequences.
